method: New full current-snapshot source review of all 198 assigned files, not a diff or test-result review. Read every assigned gateway/core implementation and test, React component/hook/library and test, stylesheet, HTML entry point and configuration. Traced HTTP/session/CSRF/WS admission, private routing and lease transitions, receipts/recovery/unknown outcomes, source/resource budgets, history and input preservation, file/Git/worktree workflows, settings/provider/account/MCP/remote/realtime/process/terminal workflows, approval schemas, keyboard/modal/mobile layout code and adequacy of corresponding tests. Re-read truncated outputs in smaller batches. Read listed current-rewrite dependencies to resolve specific lifecycle and attachment questions. Reproduced the finding by executing the exact current send handler (one TypeScript annotation removed) in an isolated Node VM, and ran only the existing targeted process-remote test file. No source, test, document or feature-evidence edits; no full suite, browser interaction, SSH, actual model, external MCP, personal home or credential access.

findings.trigger: Enter an unsent stdin draft for a running process and successfully click Send Ctrl+C or Close input stream. Also reproducible for a pending ordinary text send: edit A to B and back to A before success, or switch from process-one to process-two and type the same A before process-one success.
findings.impact: A successful control operation clears text that it never submitted. A delayed ordinary-send response can clear a newer draft revision or another selected process draft. The discarded input exists only in component state and has no recovery path. This can silently lose command/input text during normal interactive process use.
evidence: ProcessPanel.tsx:52 snapshots only the string input and calls setInput(current => current === before ? empty : current) after every successful send operation. It does not test whether text was submitted from that draft, whether the draft revision changed, or whether the selected process still owns it.

ProcessPanel.tsx:68 routes Send Ctrl+C through send(ETX) and Close input stream through send(empty, true); neither submits the editor draft. The editor remains editable while a control call is pending.

ProcessPanel.tsx:39 keys ProcessSession by epoch and connectionId; :44 uses the fixed owned-process-control workflow key. The process selector at :65 is disabled only when disconnected. Therefore changing the process during a pending call does not unmount or invalidate the original successful continuation. useWorkflow only checks component mounting before returning an accepted result.

node .work/round7/process-input-fixture.mjs executed the actual handler and reproduced four loss paths: Ctrl+C editorAfter empty with deltaBase64 Aw==; closeStdin editorAfter empty with no deltaBase64; A-to-B-to-A editorAfter empty; process-one pending send followed by process-two draft A editorAfter empty while sentParams.processHandle remained process-one. A normal unchanged send was included as a control.

The targeted existing web/tests/process-remote.test.tsx suite passes 7 tests but has no stdin control draft-preservation, edit-revision or process-selection race coverage. This passing result is not treated as proof that the affected workflow is correct.
findings.suggestedCorrection: Associate text submissions with their process owner and a monotonically changing draft revision. Clear only an unchanged submitted text draft owned by the same process. Control-only actions must preserve the editor. Add targeted interaction regressions for controls, pending edits and pending process changes.

timestampBasis: startedAt is the actual round7 interface-assignment start boundary. An explicit reviewer UTC checkpoint was captured at 2026-10-25T09:33:00Z while source review was already in progress; completedAt is the local UTC clock at evidence creation.

validations.limits: Isolated actual-source handler execution with controlled async success and simulated React setter state; no browser, real process or network.
Existing selected jsdom tests only; the confirmed loss paths are absent from their coverage.

validations.details: No old or sibling repository, Git history or prior audit report was opened. Assigned current file web/VERIFICATION.md itself embeds historical repair summaries; mandatory full review exposed that text. No linked report was opened or used as a finding source. The confirmed defect was independently found and reproduced before that assigned document was read. PROBLEM-ACCEPTANCE.md was used only as the current repository behavior contract.
